name: NIH parent announcements (investigator-initiated applications)
funder_name: National Institutes of Health

funder_name: National Institutes of Health

name: NIH Small Research Grant (R03)
funder_name: National Institutes of Health

name: NIH Research Enhancement Award Program for Health Professional Schools and Graduate Schools (R15 REAP)
funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: REAP is the R15 for health professional schools and graduate schools that have received limited NIH support. name: NIH Planning Grant (R34)

Moving from the first phase to the second depends on meeting milestones set in the application.

funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: The R35 supports an investigator's whole research programme within one institute's mission rather than a single project, and lets the investigator change direction inside that mission. name: NIH Research Program Project Grant (P01)

name: NIH Research Project Cooperative Agreement (U01)
funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: The U01 funds the same kind of discrete research project as the R01, under a cooperative agreement instead of a grant. After award, NIH scientific or programme staff assist, guide, coordinate

name: NIH Director's Early Independence Award (DP5)

funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: The Transformative Research Award supports individuals or teams proposing projects that are risky and untested but could create or overturn fundamental paradigms. It uses the R01 activity code under its own yearly notice. Budgets are not limited and the project runs up to five years. Preliminary data are not required.

name: NIH Support for Conferences and Scientific Meetings (R13)
funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: The R13 supports international, national or regional meetings, conferences and workshops that the recipient sponsors and directs. funder_name: National Institutes of Health
what: The PF5 is the structure NIH put in place of foreign subawards. name: NSF research proposal (standard proposal under the PAPPG)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: The research proposal is NSF's ordinary route to a research grant: an organisation submits a full proposal to a programme description, programme announcement or solicitation, and NSF funds it as a grant if it is recommended after merit review. Research.gov lists Research first among the proposal types it supports.

name: Rapid Response Research (RAPID)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: RAPID is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for time-sensitive work. Supplement 1 to the PAPPG sets the request ceiling at $300,000 for up to one year.

name: EArly-concept Grants for Exploratory Research (EAGER)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: EAGER is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for exploratory work in its early stages on untested but potentially transformative research ideas. Supplement 1 sets the request ceiling at $400,000 for up to two years.

name: Research Advanced by Interdisciplinary Science and Engineering (RAISE)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: RAISE is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F. NSF's 2026 core solicitations name it, with planning proposals, RAPID and EAGER, as a mechanism for preliminary or time-sensitive work.

name: Grant Opportunities for Academic Liaison with Industry (GOALI)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: GOALI is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F. In ENG a GOALI request may come with a regular proposal, as an unsolicited proposal, or as a supplemental funding request to an active award.

name: Planning proposal
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: The planning proposal is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F. Supplement 1 raised the request ceiling to $200,000 per year for up to two years.

name: Conference proposal
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: The conference proposal is a proposal type defined in PAPPG Chapter II.F for conferences, workshops and symposia. The MPS Physics solicitation states that such proposals up to $200,000 need no external review.

name: Research in Undergraduate Institutions (RUI) and Research Opportunity Awards (ROA-PUI)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: RUI supports faculty research at predominantly undergraduate institutions; ROA-PUI lets faculty from those institutions work with NSF-funded investigators elsewhere. Both run through NSF's disciplinary programmes under solicitation NSF 14-579, and the money comes from each programme's budget.

name: Core Research in Biological Sciences (BIO Core)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Biological Sciences (BIO)
what: BIO Core is the single solicitation for foundational research across biology, in three thematic areas: Foundations of Life, Living Systems, and Bioinnovation and Infrastructure.

name: CISE Future Computing Research (Future CoRe)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE)
what: Future CoRe is the CISE core-research solicitation, covering eleven programmes from Algorithmic Foundations to Software and Hardware Foundations. It was posted in July 2025 and is the current solicitation on the live opportunity page.

name: Expeditions in Computing
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE)
what: Expeditions funds large multidisciplinary teams pursuing ambitious, foundational research agendas in computing. It was reissued on August 17, 2026 as one of NSF's twelve foundational-research notices.

name: ENG: Chemical, Bioengineering, Energy, and Transport Systems (CBET)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Engineering (ENG)
what: The CBET solicitation supports foundational engineering research on chemical processes and biological systems, energy and resource management, and transport of materials and energy. Its four programmes are Chemical Process Systems; Engineering Biological and Biomedical Systems; Energy, Water, and Resource Engineering;

name: ENG: Civil, Mechanical, and Manufacturing Innovation (CMMI)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Engineering (ENG)
what: The CMMI solicitation covers four programmes: Advanced Manufacturing, Design, and Operations; Engineering for the Built Environment; Intelligent and Interactive Dynamic Systems; and Mechanics of Advanced Materials Systems.

name: ENG: Electrical, Communications, and Computing Systems (ECCS)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Engineering (ENG)
what: The ECCS solicitation supports foundational research in electrical, communications and computing systems through three programmes: Electronic, Photonic, Magnetic, and Quantum Devices; Circuits and Systems for Communications and Sensing; and Energy, Power, Control, and Learning.

name: Geosciences Core Research: Atmospheric, Geospace, Earth and Ocean Sciences (GEO Core)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Geosciences (GEO)
what: GEO Core is the single solicitation for foundational geoscience research, covering the Atmospheric and Geospace Sciences, Earth Sciences and Ocean Sciences programmes. It gathers proposals that several separate GEO opportunities used to receive.

name: MPS Astronomical Sciences Research Programs (MPS Astro)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: MPS Astro funds research in astronomical sciences through three programmes: Core Research, Technology & Instrumentation, and Innovations.

name: MPS Chemistry Research Programs (MPS Chem)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: MPS Chem funds research in nine disciplinary chemistry programmes, from Chemical Catalysis to Macromolecular, Supramolecular, and Nanochemistry.

name: MPS Materials Research Programs (MPS Materials)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: MPS Materials funds research in eight programmes: Biomaterials; Ceramics; Condensed Matter and Materials Theory; Condensed Matter Physics; Electronic and Photonic Materials; Metals and Metallic Nanostructures; Polymers; and Solid State and Materials Chemistry.

name: MPS Mathematical Sciences Research Programs (MPS MathSci)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: MPS MathSci funds research in fourteen sub-programmes: eleven disciplinary programmes from Algebra and Number Theory to Topology, plus Focused Research Groups, the Infrastructure Program and Research Training Groups.

name: MPS Physics Research Programs (MPS Physics)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: MPS Physics funds research in twelve core physics programmes and three cross-cutting ones.

name: EDU Core Research (ECR:Core)

name: Security, Privacy, and Trust in Cyberspace (SaTC 2.0)

what: SaTC 2.0 is a cross-directorate programme for research and education in cybersecurity and privacy, run by CISE with MPS, SBE and EDU. It has research (RES), education (EDU) and seed (SEED) designations.

name: Growing Convergence Research (GCR)
funder_name: U.S. National Science Foundation
what: GCR funds teams doing convergence research in two phases: Phase I for years 1-2 and, after a progress review, Phase II for years 3-5.

name: Emerging Frontiers in Research and Innovation: Wave-Based Computing (EFRI-WBC)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Engineering (ENG)
what: EFRI-WBC is ENG's 2026 Emerging Frontiers solicitation, on wave-based computing. It is one of the twelve foundational-research notices of August 17, 2026.

name: Foundational Research in Robotics (FRR)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Engineering (ENG)
what: FRR is a joint ENG and CISE programme description for fundamental robotics research. ENG lists it under both CMMI and ECCS.

name: Computational and Data-Enabled Science and Engineering (CDS&E)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: CDS&E is a programme description shared by the MPS units and two ENG units (CBET and CMMI) for computational and data-enabled research.

name: Designing Materials to Revolutionize and Engineer our Future (DMREF)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Mathematical and Physical Sciences (MPS)
what: DMREF funds teams of at least two senior/key personnel with complementary expertise in materials design, across MPS, ENG, CISE and TIP.

name: Collaborative Research in Computational Neuroscience (CRCNS)
funder_name: NSF Directorate for Computer and Information Science and Engineering (CISE)

what: This notice supports three national organisations to develop and deliver technical assistance to existing and potential health centres. Applications were taken from December 23, 2025 to March 31, 2026.

name: SAMHSA Rural Opioid Technical Assistance Centers
funder_name: Substance Abuse and Mental Health Services Administration (no research grant line found)
what: These cooperative agreements pay centres to develop and spread training and technical assistance on opioid and stimulant use in rural communities. The 2026 notice expected 11 awards of up to $650,000. It is one example of a federal technical-assistance centre that a non-profit can apply to run.

name: OJJDP Victims of Child Abuse Act Training and Technical Assistance for Child Abuse Professionals
funder_name: Office of Justice Programs (Bureau of Justice Assistance, Office for Victims of Crime, Office of Juvenile Justice and Delinquency Prevention)
what: This notice funds one national training and technical-assistance programme for child abuse professionals. It was open on the sweep date and closes October 29, 2026. name: OVW Training and Technical Assistance Initiative
funder_name: Office on Violence Against Women
what: The initiative pays providers to give specialised training and expertise on domestic violence, dating violence, sexual assault and stalking to OVW grantees, potential grantees and subgrantees. OVW's FY 2026 list marks it as not currently accepting applications.

funder_name: National Endowment for the Humanities
what: These grants fund 20-year term endowments to support long-term work in the humanities, matched one to one with non-federal money. funder_name: National Endowment for the Humanities

funder_name: Institute of Museum and Library Services
what: Museums Empowered funds projects that use learning and training to bring about change and growth inside a museum, in digital technology, evaluation and organisational management. The FY 2027 notice is available and applications are due November 13, 2026.

name: IMLS Museum Grants for African American History and Culture
funder_name: Institute of Museum and Library Services
what: These grants fund projects that develop museum professionals, build institutional capacity and widen access to museum and archival collections. The FY 2027 notice is available and applications are due November 13, 2026.

name: IMLS Museum Grants for American Latino History and Culture
funder_name: Institute of Museum and Library Services
what: These grants fund projects that build the capacity of American Latino history and culture museums to serve their communities. The FY 2027 notice is available and applications are due November 13, 2026.

funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: Save America's Treasures pays for bricks-and-mortar preservation of nationally significant historic properties and for conservation of nationally significant collections. name: National Park Service Historically Black Colleges and Universities Grants (Historic Preservation Fund)
funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: These grants document, preserve and stabilise historic structures on the campuses of Historically Black Colleges and Universities, and may also pay for survey, National Register nomination and preservation planning for a campus. The FY2025 competition closed July 28, 2026, with 16 awards expected from $11,000,000.

funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)

name: National Park Service History of Equal Rights Grants (Historic Preservation Fund)
funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: These grants preserve sites related to the struggle of all people to achieve equal rights in America, paying for architectural services, historic structure reports, preservation plans and physical preservation of structures. The 2026 notice combined FY2025 and FY2026 money and closed July 21, 2026.

name: National Park Service Underrepresented Communities Grants (Historic Preservation Fund)
funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: These grants pay for surveys and nominations of historic sites associated with communities underrepresented in the National Register of Historic Places. The FY2025 competition closed July 7, 2026, with 15 awards expected from $1,250,000.

name: National Park Service Paul Bruhn Historic Revitalization Grants
funder_name: National Park Service, State, Tribal, Local, Plans & Grants Division (Historic Preservation Fund grants)
what: Paul Bruhn grants fund a prime grantee to run a subgrant programme that rehabilitates historic buildings in rural communities. A prime cannot use the money for its own properties or apply for individual buildings. The 2026 notice, with $17,000,000, was due June 23, 2026.

name: NHPRC State Board Programming Grants
funder_name: National Historical Publications and Records Commission
what: These grants strengthen the archival network through State Historical Records Advisory Boards, which may spend them on board administration, regrants to archival repositories, professional development for archivists and consultation services. The last deadline was May 7, 2025, for awards running January 1, 2026 to Dece

name: NHPRC Capacity Building for HBCU Archives
funder_name: National Historical Publications and Records Commission
what: This programme funded archival capacity building at Historically Black Colleges and Universities: training, processing, preservation, discovery and access for their archival collections. Its one notice found closed November 7, 2024; the Commission's announcements page on the sweep date does not list it.

name: HRSA Health Center Capital Development Grants
funder_name: Health Resources and Services Administration (maternal and child health research line)
what: Capital Development Grants support health centres' efforts to expand their capacity to provide primary and preventive care to medically underserved communities. name: USDA Community Facilities Technical Assistance and Training Grant
funder_name: USDA Rural Development
what: This grant pays for help identifying and planning for community facility needs and preparing the reports and surveys needed to ask for financial assistance. The maximum grant is $150,000. The application window was shown as closed on the sweep date, with applications to be taken after a funding notice is published.

name: FEMA Building Resilient Infrastructure and Communities (BRIC), in outline
funder_name: Federal Emergency Management Agency (preparedness grants)
what: BRIC is FEMA's pre-disaster mitigation grant programme; states, the District of Columbia, territories and tribes apply, and local governments, special districts and tribes are subapplicants. name: DOE Renew America's Nonprofits (energy efficiency grants for non-profit buildings)
funder_name: U.S. Department of Energy (as a research grant-maker)
what: Renew America's Nonprofits pays for materials that cut energy or fuel use in buildings owned and operated by 501(c)(3) non-profits. In its one round, in 2023, the Department offered $45 million to 5 to 15 prime recipients, each a non-profit that assembles a portfolio of buildings and makes subawards of up to $200,000.

name: NEH Humanities Initiatives (colleges and universities, and the HBCU, HSI, TCU and community college variants)
funder_name: National Endowment for the Humanities
what: Humanities Initiatives grants strengthen the teaching and study of the humanities at institutions of higher education by developing new humanities programmes, educational resources or coursework, or improving existing ones. funder_name: National Institute on Minority Health and Health Disparities

name: Native American Research Centers for Health (NARCH), S06 centre awards
funder_name: National Institute of General Medical Sciences
what: NARCH funds federally recognized American Indian and Alaska Native Tribes and tribal entities to support health-related research, research career enhancement and research infrastructure enhancement. name: USDA Rural Development Tribal College Initiative Grants
funder_name: USDA Rural Development
what: Tribal College Initiative Grants pay for capital improvements to the educational facilities of the 1994 land-grant tribal colleges and for equipment. Uses named on the page include schools, libraries, dormitories, renovations and vehicles. Applications are taken all year through the local Rural Development office.

name: NIFA Hatch Act capacity grants (State Agricultural Experiment Stations)
funder_name: National Institute of Food and Agriculture
what: Hatch Act funds pay for agricultural research programmes at the State Agricultural Experiment Stations in the 50 states, the District of Columbia and the U.S. insular areas. The money is divided by a statutory formula, not by competition; each station answers a yearly request for applications to receive its share. Hatc

name: AmeriCorps Volunteer Generation Fund
funder_name: AmeriCorps (Corporation for National and Community Service)
what: The Volunteer Generation Fund invests in volunteer engagement practices that strengthen an organisation's ability to recruit and keep volunteers, including the capacity of volunteer connector organisations. Only State Service Commissions may apply to AmeriCorps. The FY 2026 notice was posted April 1, 2026 and closed Ap

name: SBA Program for Investment in Microentrepreneurs (PRIME)
funder_name: U.S. Small Business Administration (grants to resource partners)
what: PRIME makes grants to private non-profit microenterprise development organisations that give assistance and guidance to disadvantaged microentrepreneurs. The FY 2026 notice, SB-OCAPR-26-001, was posted July 15, 2026 and closed August 12, 2026. The previous notices in the Grants.gov listing date from 2019.

name: Simons Collaborations in Mathematics and the Physical Sciences
funder_name: Simons Foundation
what: A Simons Collaboration is a grant to a group of investigators under a collaboration director, aimed at a fundamental question in mathematics, theoretical physics or theoretical computer science. The 2027 round was open on 2026-10-04 with a letter of intent due October 29, 2026.

name: Simons Foundation Pivot Fellowship
funder_name: Simons Foundation
what: The Pivot Fellowship pays a faculty member with a record in one field to spend a year training in a new discipline with a mentor. The competition was marked closed on 2026-10-04; the last deadline was May 14, 2026 and no date for the next round is given.

name: Sloan Research Fellowships
funder_name: Alfred P. Sloan Foundation
what: A two-year, $75,000 fellowship for early-career faculty in chemistry, computer science, Earth system science, economics, mathematics, neuroscience, physics or a related field. The nomination period for the 2027 fellowships closed on September 15, 2026.

name: W. M. Keck Foundation Research Program
funder_name: W. M. Keck Foundation
what: Grants of about $1 million for basic research in science and engineering that is distinctive and novel in approach. An institution may send up to three applications in each of two cycles a year; the next deadline after 2026-10-04 is December 7, 2026.

name: Cottrell Scholar Award
funder_name: Research Corporation for Science Advancement
what: A three-year, $120,000 award to an early-career tenure-track faculty member in chemistry, physics or astronomy, for research and teaching together. The round with the July 1, 2026 deadline was closed on 2026-10-04.

name: Camille Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Awards
funder_name: The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation
what: A $100,000 unrestricted research grant to an early-career faculty member in the chemical sciences in a Ph.D.-granting department. The next deadline after 2026-10-04 is February 4, 2027.

name: Henry Dreyfus Teacher-Scholar Awards
funder_name: The Camille and Henry Dreyfus Foundation
what: A $75,000 unrestricted research grant to a chemistry faculty member in a department that does not grant a doctorate. The 2026 deadline was August 6, 2026, with the announcement due early November 2026.

name: Packard Fellowships for Science and Engineering
funder_name: The David and Lucile Packard Foundation
what: A five-year, $875,000 fellowship for faculty in the first three years of their first appointment, open only to nominees of 50 invited universities. The 2026 round closed in April 2026; no guidelines for a 2027 round were found on 2026-10-04.

name: HHMI Investigator Program
funder_name: Howard Hughes Medical Institute
what: An HHMI Investigator is employed by HHMI, which pays full salary, benefits and a research budget, while the scientist keeps an academic appointment and laboratory at the home institution. The competition is held every 5 years; the next opens September 28, 2027.

name: HHMI Freeman Hrabowski Scholars Program
funder_name: Howard Hughes Medical Institute
what: Early-career faculty become HHMI employees with full salary, benefits and an annual research budget for up to 10 years, keeping their appointment and laboratory at the host institution. The 2028 competition, held jointly with the Hanna H. Gray Fellows competition, opens November 3, 2026 and closes December 15, 2026.

name: HHMI Hanna H. Gray Fellows Program
funder_name: Howard Hughes Medical Institute
what: Support for a postdoctoral scientist in the basic biological and biomedical sciences for up to two years, with a route into the Freeman Hrabowski Scholars Program on taking up a qualifying faculty post. The 2028 competition opens November 3, 2026 and closes December 15, 2026.

name: Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Awards for Medical Scientists (CAMS)
funder_name: Burroughs Wellcome Fund
what: A five-year, $700,000 award that carries a physician-scientist from advanced postdoctoral or fellowship training into the first faculty years. The 2026 deadline was Sep 30, 2026; the page still read "Now Accepting Applications" on 2026-10-04.

name: Burroughs Wellcome Fund Career Awards at the Scientific Interface (CASI)
funder_name: Burroughs Wellcome Fund
what: A five-year, $560,000 award for a postdoctoral scientist trained in the physical, mathematical or computational sciences or engineering who is moving into biology and towards a faculty post. The letter-of-intent deadline for this cycle was Aug 14, 2026; full applications from those invited are due January 11, 2027.

name: Pew Scholars Program in the Biomedical Sciences
funder_name: The Pew Charitable Trusts
what: Four years of flexible research support for an assistant professor in the first years of running an independent laboratory, open only to one nominee from each participating institution. Eligibility for the 2027 award was fixed as of Sept. 3, 2026, so that round was closed on 2026-10-04.

name: Demonstrating Health Solutions Science in Action (Doris Duke Foundation and the Pathways for Health Research Collective)
funder_name: Doris Duke Foundation
what: A call for three-year projects that apply evidence-based health solutions science in the United States and measure the effect on health. Pre-proposals are due November 18, 2026; the Doris Duke Foundation handles intake and review for a group of funders.

name: American Heart Association Career Development Award
funder_name: American Heart Association
what: A three-year, non-renewable award for a health or academic professional in the early years of a first professional appointment. The proposal deadline is December 1, 2026.

name: American Cancer Society Research Scholar Grants
funder_name: American Cancer Society
what: A project grant of up to $215,000 a year for up to four years for an independent investigator within 8 years of the first independent appointment, in an ACS priority research area. Applications are taken at two deadlines a year; the next after 2026-10-04 is December 1.

name: Spencer Foundation Research Grants on Education: Small
funder_name: Spencer Foundation
what: Field-initiated education research projects with budgets up to $50,000, lasting one to five years. Applications were marked "Now closed" on 2026-10-04 and the page showed no next date.

name: Spencer Foundation Research Grants on Education: Large
funder_name: Spencer Foundation
what: Field-initiated education research projects with budgets from $125,000 to $500,000 in three tiers, lasting up to 5 years. Applications were marked "Now closed" on 2026-10-04; from 2026 there is one cycle a year.

name: Spencer Foundation Research-Practice Partnerships
funder_name: Spencer Foundation
what: Grants of up to $400,000 over up to three years for partnerships between researchers and practitioners in education. The 2026 pre-proposal deadline had passed on 2026-10-04; the October 28, 2026 date on the foundation's list is for invited full proposals.

name: Russell Sage Foundation Core Research Grants
funder_name: Russell Sage Foundation
what: Grants for social science research in the foundation's priority areas: Trustee Grants up to $200,000 and Presidential Grants up to $50,000, generally for two years. The next letter-of-inquiry deadline after 2026-10-04 is October 28, 2026, for the Social, Political and Economic Inequality and Future of Work programmes a

name: Russell Sage Foundation Sheldon Danziger Pipeline Grants
funder_name: Russell Sage Foundation
what: A competition, run with the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation, for faculty who have not had support from the Russell Sage Foundation before. The 2026 deadline is Wednesday, October 21, 2026, 2pm ET.

name: William T. Grant Scholars Program
funder_name: William T. Grant Foundation
what: A five-year, $425,000 award for an early-career researcher's research and mentoring plan that stretches the researcher's expertise. The 2026 competition was closed on 2026-10-04; dates for the next are to be posted in January 2027.

name: William T. Grant Foundation Research Grants on Reducing Inequality
funder_name: William T. Grant Foundation
what: Grants for research on programmes, policies or practices that reduce inequality in the academic, social, behavioral or economic outcomes of young people ages 5-25. The 2026 cycles were closed on 2026-10-04; 2027 deadlines are to be posted in November 2026.

name: Andrew Carnegie Fellows Program
funder_name: Carnegie Corporation of New York
what: A grant of up to $200,000 to a scholar for a research project of up to two years on political polarization. A new three-year nomination cycle begins in 2027, for fellowships starting June to September 2027; the page read gave no nomination deadline, so the state of the round on 2026-10-04 is not confirmed.

name: Guggenheim Fellowships (United States and Canada competition)
funder_name: John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation
what: A fellowship of six to twelve months for a mid-career individual in any field of scholarship or any art form. The 2027 competition closed on September 15, 2026; Fellows are announced in late April 2027.

name: ACLS Fellowship Program
funder_name: American Council of Learned Societies
what: Fellowships for individual scholars in the humanities and social sciences, including independent scholars, paid for mainly from the ACLS endowment. The 2026 deadline was September 17, 2026.

name: Mellon/ACLS Dissertation Innovation Fellowships
funder_name: American Council of Learned Societies
what: Fellowships for doctoral students whose dissertation projects use new methods, formats or collaborations; ACLS runs the competition and "the program is made possible by a grant from the Mellon Foundation". The deadline is October 28, 2026.

name: 100&Change
funder_name: John D. and Catherine T. MacArthur Foundation
what: 100&Change is a competition for a single $100 million grant to one proposal that addresses a critical problem. Three cycles have run; the third closed to applications on September 5, 2024 and named Sentinel as its award recipient.

name: Exploring Equitable Futures (RWJF open call for ideas)
funder_name: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation
what: Exploring Equitable Futures is the foundation's standing open call for proposals, which closes and reopens each year. In 2024 it made 8 grants, about 1 percent of the applications received.

name: Evidence for Action: Rapid Response Research
funder_name: Robert Wood Johnson Foundation
what: A single call issued in August 2025 to 'Support timely, actionable health equity research that has been interrupted by shifts in federal funding'. Applicants had to have lost federal funding for a health equity research project and document the termination.

name: Knight Cities Challenge
funder_name: John S. and James L. Knight Foundation
what: An open call for projects in the 26 Knight communities that strengthen local news, expand economic opportunity or deepen community connection through arts and culture. The foundation relaunched it in 2026 with $10 million for two cohorts over three years.

name: Mellon Higher Learning Program Open Call for Concepts
funder_name: Mellon Foundation
what: An open call from the foundation's Higher Learning programme for research and curricular projects in the humanities on set themes; the 2026 themes were 'Unruly Intelligences' and 'Normalization and Its Discontents'. The foundation committed $10 million to the 2026 call.

name: Mellon Humanities in Place
funder_name: Mellon Foundation
what: Humanities in Place funds programming by community groups on cultural heritage, work on overlooked communities and regions, and cultural heritage sites. It is the one Mellon programme found to take applications at any time.

name: Arnold Ventures request for proposals: Causal Research on the Impacts of K-12 School Policies
funder_name: Arnold Ventures
what: A request for proposals issued in September 2026 for causal studies of the effects of K-12 school policies. It is one of two requests listed as open on 2026-10-04.

name: Yield Giving Open Call
funder_name: Yield Giving (MacKenzie Scott)
what: The one open application Yield Giving has held: 'an open call completed in 2024 with an online application'. It selected 361 community-led non-profits from more than 6,000 applicants.

name: Walmart Spark Good Local Grants
funder_name: Walmart and the Walmart Foundation
what: Small cash grants awarded by individual Walmart stores, Sam's Clubs and distribution centres to organisations in their communities through an open application. Walmart calls it the only one of its programmes that takes open applications through the year.

name: Bank of America Charitable Foundation local grants (requests for proposals)
funder_name: Bank of America Charitable Foundation
what: Two requests for proposals a year for non-profits in the bank's local markets, one for basic needs and income creation and one for stable housing and empowering communities. Grants are for one year.

name: Home Depot Foundation Veteran Housing Grants
funder_name: The Home Depot Foundation
what: Grants to non-profits for new construction or rehabilitation of multifamily, permanent supportive housing for veterans. Awards typically range from $100,000 to $500,000.

name: Lowe's Foundation Gable Grants
funder_name: Lowe's Foundation
what: Grants to community and technical colleges and non-profit organisations for skilled trades training, part of a $250 million investment to train 250,000 tradespeople by 2035. Only the round for community and technical colleges is an open application.

name: Silicon Valley Community Foundation Community Action Grants
funder_name: Silicon Valley Community Foundation
what: The community foundation's annual request for proposals for non-profits in its region. The 2026 round has closed and the page points to a 2027 round.
